title: Jury recommendations
article: A coroner's jury looking into the death of a prisoner says overall safety would be enhanced if two police officers transported distraught people to hospital.
The jury examining the death of Mladen Cujko also recommended staffing levels at RCMP detachments be reviewed to establish a minimum standard, a process already being studied at the national level.
Pathologist Laurel Gray testified that Cujko, 33, died of a cardiac arrest brought on by five times the minimum lethal limit of cocaine in his body.
RCMP picked up Cujko on Aug. 21 after callers reported that a distraught man was running in and out of traffic.
Const. Murray Bayles started driving him to the Royal Jubilee Hospital for a psychiatric assessment when Cujko became agitated and started trying to kick out the rear window.
After a struggle, Cujko stopped breathing. A paramedic tried to revive him but was unsuccessful.
